title: UI: group medication features in a Medication flyout and clarify labels
body:
## Problem

Following completion of [Plan 22](https://github.com/datagen24/victual/blob/master/docs/plans/22-medication-tracking.md), the server web UI exposes **Consumption recipes**, **Consumption inbox**, and **Prescription refills** as separate sidebar entries. These belong together, and the consumption terminology is unclear in a medication workflow. “Consumption recipes” also sounds like food recipes.

## Requested change

Add a single **Medication** sidebar entry with a flyout containing the medication features delivered by Plan 22. Review the related visible wording, including the inbox, so navigation and page labels use clear, consistent language.

Proposed wording for implementation review:

| Current label | Proposed label |
| --- | --- |
| Consumption recipes | Medication presets |
| Consumption inbox | Medication inbox |
| Prescription refills | Refills (within Medication) |

“Medication presets” describes saved product-and-quantity combinations used to record consumption. The wording should also make sense for vitamins and supplements. These names are starting suggestions; the requested outcome is clearer language throughout the medication UI.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Medication is a single sidebar entry whose flyout groups the existing recipe/preset, inbox, and refill destinations.
- [ ] Replace “Consumption recipes” with a clearer user-facing name and improve the inbox label; apply the chosen wording consistently to navigation, page titles, relevant actions, tooltips, and translatable strings.
- [ ] Existing permissions and feature visibility remain effective, and the active medication destination is identifiable.
- [ ] The flyout works with keyboard navigation, collapsed navigation, and mobile layouts.
- [ ] Existing medication workflows and direct links continue to work. This is navigation and wording polish; internal API/schema terminology need not change.

## Implementation pointers

The three current entries are adjacent in `views/layout/default.blade.php`, linking to `/consumptionrecipes`, `/consumptioninbox`, and `/consumptionrefills`. Related Plan 22 implementation: #698, #700, #701.

title: Uploading a userfile under an existing unreferenced name reveals that the name exists

milestone.description: Follow-ups found while building 0.5.0 that do not block the first production release: presentation residuals, low-severity disclosures and CI hygiene. Lands after 0.5.0 and before 0.6.0.

body:
A residual of #905/#920, documented as "Not covered" in ADR-0048 item 9 (PR #978).

## What happens

Uploading a userfile under a name that already exists, but that no record references, answers 400. That tells the caller the name exists, even when they could never read the file, for example one left behind by a record they had no access to.

The same item also accepts that a caller allowed to make the write can attach a file nothing references. Nothing records whether an unreferenced file was just uploaded or left behind by an earlier owner.

## Expected

Decide whether the existence answer matters. One option: answer an upload to a taken name the same way whether or not the caller could read it, or namespace uploads per uploader. Then update ADR-0048 item 9.

## Why this does not block 0.5.0

Gate R1 is about reading or rewriting protected file contents, and #978 closes that. This is a name-existence signal only, and ADR-0048 already records it.

title: Calendar API 500 includes the user-supplied event title in its body

labels.name: php
labels.description: Pull requests that update php code

milestone.description: Follow-ups found while building 0.5.0 that do not block the first production release: presentation residuals, low-severity disclosures and CI hygiene. Lands after 0.5.0 and before 0.6.0.

body:
Follow-up recorded during #801 (decision D4, 2026-10-13): keep and document the existing behaviour, and assess the runtime disclosure separately. This issue is that assessment.

## What happens

`controllers/Api/CalendarApiController.php` (lines 192–198 on master) throws `HttpInternalServerErrorException` when an internal calendar event source returns an event without `event_type`/`entity_id`. The message appends the event's `title`:

```php
'Calendar event is missing event_type/entity_id required for a stable UID (#511)'
. (isset($event['title']) ? ": {$event['title']}" : '')
```

The title is user-supplied text, such as a chore, product or meal plan name, so it reaches the 500 response body.

## Expected

Decide whether the 500 body should carry user-supplied text. If it shouldn't, log the title (or the event type and source) server-side, and answer with the fixed message only.

## Why this does not block 0.5.0

The branch is reachable only when Victual's own event sources produce a malformed event; it guards an internal invariant (#511). A caller who reaches it is already allowed to see the calendar, and so the title.

title: prose-baseline-prune fails daily: it pushes to master, which requires a pull request

milestone.description: Follow-ups found while building 0.5.0 that do not block the first production release: presentation residuals, low-severity disclosures and CI hygiene. Lands after 0.5.0 and before 0.6.0.

body:
## What happens

The scheduled `prose-baseline-prune` workflow has failed every day since at least 2026-10-15. These runs all fail:
- [38728483849](https://github.com/datagen24/victual/actions/runs/38728483849)
- [38894184659](https://github.com/datagen24/victual/actions/runs/38894184659)
- [39026410261](https://github.com/datagen24/victual/actions/runs/39026410261)
- [39122417217](https://github.com/datagen24/victual/actions/runs/39122417217)

Every step passes up to and including the prune: the run removes the resolved entries (889 on 2026-10-16) and `audit.py --check` passes. The last step, `Commit if the baseline changed`, fails because it runs `git push origin master`, and the repository rule requires every change to master to go through a pull request.

So `.devtools/vale/baseline.json` is never pruned. The repository's Vale hook reports this on every commit: "889 resolved or changed baseline entries are stale; the scheduled prune on master removes them."

## Expected

The prune lands. For example, the job opens or updates a pull request from a fixed branch instead of pushing to master. Alternatively, the workflow is changed or removed and the hook message is corrected.

## Why this does not block 0.5.0

It is CI hygiene. Release checks and new-finding detection are unaffected.

title: Consume stores any integer recipe_id, including negative ids and ids no recipe has

labels.name: php
labels.description: Pull requests that update php code

milestone.description: Follow-ups found while building 0.5.0 that do not block the first production release: presentation residuals, low-severity disclosures and CI hygiene. Lands after 0.5.0 and before 0.6.0.

body:
Found while closing #950 (PR #976 and PR #977).

## What happens

`POST /api/stock/products/{id}/consume` and the by-barcode consume route store any integer `recipe_id` exactly as sent, including negative values and ids no recipe has. #976 made unusable values (`"2 "`, `1e309`, a 400-digit number) answer 400, but an integer is passed through.

| `recipe_id` sent | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `-2` | 200, consumed, `stock_log.recipe_id = -2` |
| `-2147483648` | 200, consumed, stored as sent (pinned as current behaviour in `NumericStringAcceptanceTest` by PR #977) |
| an id with no recipe | consumed and stored (from the code: `StockApiController::ConsumeProduct` passes it to `StockService::ConsumeProduct` with no lookup, and `stock_log.recipe_id` has no foreign key) |

#950's closing comment records that it does not cover the negative case.

## Expected

A `recipe_id` that names no recipe answers 400 and books nothing, the way shopping-list remove now answers a negative `product_id`.

## Why this does not block 0.5.0

The rows stay readable, and nothing reads `stock_log.recipe_id` in a way that fails on a dangling id. This is a validation gap, not gate R2's unreadable-row class.

title: Decide whether ApiResponse encodes with JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR (from #844)
body:
Split out of #844's third done-when item ("Decide separately"), 2026-10-13. Decision needed; nothing is proposed for implementation yet.

`BaseApiController::ApiResponse()` (`controllers/Api/BaseApiController.php` ~:36-44) calls `json_encode($data)` without checking the result. For a value `json_encode` cannot encode (INF, NAN, invalid UTF-8), it returns `false`, the write fails, and the client receives a 500 with an empty body. The handler has already committed any writes the route made. PR #911 closes the lookup path that #844 found; other routes can still reach this path with other data.

## Options

- (a) Encode with `JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR`, so an unencodable body becomes the standard 500 error body with a logged cause. This changes the failure body on every route (ADR-0005), not the success shape.
- (b) Keep the current behaviour and rely on per-path validation, as #844 did for the lookup.

Either way, writes that a route has already committed stay committed. Moving the encode inside the transaction is a separate and larger question.

Related: #844, #801 (documenting the production 500).

title: Battery and equipment rework: residual battery authorization findings
body:
The maintainer intends to rework batteries together with equipment (tool packs, chargers, racks). ADR-0043 (accepted 2026-10-12, open question 2) keeps battery writes unchanged until then. This issue collects the battery authorization findings that were deliberately left for that rework, so that closing #897 does not lose them. Nothing here is scheduled.

## Residual findings (master `01c3fa1b`, code reading)

1. **`MASTER_DATA_EDIT` writes batteries it cannot read** (#897, closed as decided by ADR-0043 on 2026-10-13). A `MASTER_DATA_EDIT`-only caller can POST, PUT and DELETE `/api/objects/batteries` (`controllers/Api/GenericEntityApiController.php:80, 430, 253`). It cannot read the rows back.
2. **Existence oracle.** PUT and DELETE on an absent battery id return 404 (`GenericEntityApiController.php:452, 266, 277`), and on an existing id 204. A caller without `BATTERIES_VIEW` therefore learns which battery ids exist.
3. **Cascading delete.** Deleting a battery cascades to its whole charge history and its userfield values (`trg_cascade_battery_removal`, `db/pgsql/baseline/06_triggers_c.sql:128-144`). It is authorized by `MASTER_DATA_EDIT` alone, which cannot view that history.
4. **Charge-cycle write read-back:** filed separately as #908.

Precedent for the rework: equipment writes already require `EQUIPMENT` (`GenericEntityApiController.php:63-64, 245`).

None of these findings is fixed. Each needs a decision in the rework.

title: Subprocess test helpers read stdout before stderr and deadlock on more than 64 KB of stderr
body:
Test helpers that start a PHP subprocess read its stdout to EOF before reading stderr. A child that writes more than the 64 KB pipe buffer to stderr blocks, never closes stdout, and deadlocks the test run while holding database locks.

## Where

- `tests/Pgsql/InfluxPermanentRejectionTest.php`: `Drain()` (~:176)
- `tests/Pgsql/OutboxClaimConcurrencyTest.php`: `finishSubprocess()` (~:213)
- About 75 files under `tests/Pgsql/` use the same stdout-then-stderr pattern

## Evidence

On 2026-10-12 an `mqttcoverage` run hung for 2.5 hours. A second hang was diagnosed from `/proc`:
- `outbox-claim-subprocess-helper.php drain` was blocked in `anon_pipe_write`;
- its database session sat "idle in transaction";
- PHPUnit waited on stdout.

The child had logged about 78 KB (399 `error_log` lines for a 201-row probe).

## Failure scenario

Any test, or future test, whose child writes more than 64 KB to stderr hangs the suite indefinitely instead of failing. In CI that runs until the job timeout; locally it holds the shared runner lock.

## Possible direction

Read both pipes together (`stream_select`, or `stream_set_blocking(false)` with a loop), or send the child's stderr to a temp file, in one shared helper used by every subprocess test.

## How this was found

Reported by an independent validator during the 2026-10-12 audit remediation (issues #846–#868), while it reviewed PR #874 (#854).

title: ADR-0019 does not list the Resolve() validation refusal as a dead-letter cause
body:
ADR-0019's list of dead-letter causes does not include one the code already uses: `PrintAttemptService::Claim()` dead-letters a job when `Resolve()` throws a `LabelValidationException`.

## Where

- `services/Labels/PrintAttemptService.php`: `Claim()`, the `catch (LabelValidationException)` around `Resolve()`
- `docs/adr/0019-label-printers-are-master-data.md`: Offline behaviour (the closed list of dead-letter causes)

## Evidence

ADR-0019 lists an unreadable payload (migration 0259), a deleted printer (decision item 4) and, since the 2026-10-12 amendment in PR #881, a render request that can no longer produce an artifact. A `Resolve()` validation refusal is neither an unreadable payload in 0259's sense nor any of the others.

## Failure scenario

There is no runtime failure. The record and the code disagree, so a reader of ADR-0019 cannot tell that a job can be set aside for a resolution refusal.

## Possible direction

Either amend ADR-0019 to name this cause and when it applies, or show that the case is covered by "unreadable payload" and say so in the code comment.

## How this was found

Reported by an independent validator during the 2026-10-12 audit remediation (issues #846–#868), while it reviewed PR #881 (the ADR-0019 amendment).

title: Audit and bring the REST API specification into full OpenAPI 3.2 compliance

milestone.description: Later feature release: OAuth then federation; installation country, canonical/scoped barcode resolution and web onboarding, each behind its own design/ADR gates. Full API audit remains later work. These are not requirements for 0.5.0.

body:
Bring `victual.openapi.json` and the document served by `/api/openapi/specification` into compliance with [OpenAPI 3.2.0](https://swagger.io/specification/v3.2/), and verify that the document describes the API's actual request and response contracts.

## Starting evidence

Requested 2026-10-12 after an external Level 1 Spec Audit reported High risk, a 45% Spec Integrity Score, 180 endpoints, 208 missing error response specifications/schema validation gaps, and 12 stateful E2E scenarios under its TDS standard. These are supplied scan results, not independently reproduced findings. The detailed report, counting rules and TDS definition were not supplied. Do not treat those totals as confirmed OAS violations.

The clean working copy at `8fd7660754664b6c9361b328b178bb7b93c8265f` currently declares `openapi: 3.1.0`. The initial audit will distinguish normative OAS violations, migration requirements, API contract drift, and optional documentation improvements. Missing optional OAS features alone are not failures.

## Completion criteria

- [ ] Record a reproducible audit against a named commit, including both the source document and the served document's transformations.
- [ ] Declare OAS 3.2.0 after validating the document and its schema dialect; verify references, parameters, request bodies, responses, examples and security declarations.
- [ ] Map implemented operations and known success/error outcomes to their documented status, media type, headers and body schema. Preserve ADR-0005's wire-contract constraints; document discrepancies before deciding which side changes.
- [ ] Open a linked sub-issue for each verified deviation or coherent repeated defect, with evidence and acceptance criteria. Reuse existing issues where they already own the finding.
- [ ] Add an OAS 3.2-capable validation gate and demonstrate that intentionally invalid fixtures fail. Keep runtime contract verification separate from structural specification validation.
- [ ] Verify the served documentation UI and Victual-owned client/tool consumers against the 3.2 document.
- [ ] Reconcile the external scan's totals when its detailed report and counting rules are available; independently define and verify applicable stateful workflows.
- [ ] Close verified findings and record final validation commands, tool versions, results and remaining limitations.

## Existing related findings

- #787: inherited stock-route schemas and recipe fulfillment omit fields the server sends.
- #648: generic entity responses decode under schemas belonging to other entities.

Initial audit findings and native sub-issue links will be added below. This issue authorizes investigation and tracks remediation; it does not accept Proposed ADRs or authorize unrelated wire changes.

title: Design: external identity provider (OIDC and SAML) with Authentik as the reference IdP

milestone.description: Later feature release: OAuth then federation; installation country, canonical/scoped barcode resolution and web onboarding, each behind its own design/ADR gates. Full API audit remains later work. These are not requirements for 0.5.0.

body:
## Problem

Household members should be able to sign in to Victual, and authorize API and MCP clients, with an identity held by an external identity provider rather than a separate Victual password. The target is the maintainer's home lab, which runs **Authentik**, but the design should work with any standards-compliant IdP (Keycloak, Authelia, Entra, Google).

This depends on the OAuth API-access issue (see "Depends on" below), which defines how Victual validates tokens and maps them to users. This issue adds federation on top of it.

## Goal

- **OIDC** as the primary protocol: Victual (or its sidecar) acts as a relying party for interactive login, and as a resource server accepting IdP-issued access tokens for API and MCP callers.
- **SAML 2.0** as a secondary protocol for IdPs or environments that offer nothing else. Authentik supports both, so SAML can be tested against the same instance. Whether SAML is worth shipping at all is an open question, not an assumption.
- Authentik is the reference IdP and the integration test target.

## Scope

- **Discovery and configuration.** `.well-known/openid-configuration`, JWKS fetching and caching with rotation, issuer and audience pinning. Configuration via environment variables and the Helm chart (ADR-0038), with secrets from the existing secret mechanism; nothing stored in the database that a restore could leak.
- **Identity mapping.** Stable key is the `iss` + `sub` pair, never email. Decide: just-in-time provisioning vs. pre-created users only vs. both; behaviour when an IdP email matches an existing local user; account linking and unlinking.
- **Authorization mapping.** IdP groups/claims to Victual roles and permission grants (ADR-0018). Must not let an IdP claim grant more than the maintainer-approved mapping, and must define what happens when a claim disappears (permissions revoked at next token or next login?). Interacts with ADR-0014 (administering a user is a subset question).
- **Sessions.** Browser login via authorization code + PKCE; logout, back-channel/front-channel logout, session lifetime relative to IdP session.
- **Non-browser callers.** IdP-issued tokens accepted on `/api` and on the MCP sidecar; service accounts via client credentials; device flow for CLIs.
- **Local fallback.** Local username/password login must remain available (break-glass when the IdP is down, installs with no IdP). Decide whether it can be disabled once OIDC is configured.
- **Failure modes.** IdP unreachable, JWKS rotation mid-request, clock skew, token for the wrong audience, user deleted at the IdP but holding a live token.
- **Authentik walkthrough** in `docs/manual`: provider, application, scope mappings, group claims, redirect URIs.

## Open questions

- Is Victual the OIDC relying party, or does it only validate tokens and leave browser login to a forward-auth proxy (Authentik outpost / Traefik)? The latter is much less code but makes Victual's own user model dependent on proxy headers, which is a trust-boundary question for the ADR.
- SAML: ship it, document the proxy route instead, or defer until someone needs it? PHP SAML libraries carry a notable security-maintenance burden (XML signature handling).
- Per-user API keys and local passwords alongside OIDC users: do keys remain tied to a user row, and can an IdP-provisioned user create them?
- Multi-IdP, or exactly one configured IdP per install?
- What does the MCP sidecar need from the IdP beyond token validation (it must stay stateless; ADR-0039 reads its configuration from Victual)?
- Audit: do IdP login events belong in the existing audit trail, and with what identity?

## Deliverables

1. Design discussion here, informed by the answers to the first issue's authorization-server question.
2. **An ADR** for the federation architecture (new decision). It may be one record with the OAuth ADR or a second; decide once the design settles, but it must not be accepted before the OAuth one.
3. A plan under `docs/plans/` after the ADR is accepted. No code before then.

## Depends on

- The OAuth API-access issue (#770).

## Related

- ADR-0007, ADR-0014, ADR-0018, ADR-0038, ADR-0039, ADR-0044
- `docs/mcp-interface-spec.md` §4.1 (future-state note for a household IdP)

title: Design: OAuth 2.1 access tokens for API and MCP, replacing static API keys as the primary credential

milestone.description: Later feature release: OAuth then federation; installation country, canonical/scoped barcode resolution and web onboarding, each behind its own design/ADR gates. Full API audit remains later work. These are not requirements for 0.5.0.

body:
## Problem

Every non-browser caller authenticates with a long-lived static secret. A Victual API key is sent as `VICTUAL-API-KEY` (or, for the MCP sidecar, as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, which is the same key forwarded). That is the upstream grocy model and it has the usual weaknesses:

- It never expires unless someone remembers to revoke it, and it is a bearer secret: whoever holds it is its owner, with no proof of which client is presenting it.
- There is no consent step, no refresh, and no per-client identity. Two clients sharing a key are indistinguishable in the audit trail.
- MCP clients that implement the MCP authorization framework (OAuth 2.1 resource server, RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata) cannot connect without a bridge. [`docs/mcp-interface-spec.md`](../blob/master/docs/mcp-interface-spec.md) §4.1 records this as a deliberate v1 gap: the sidecar returns `404` for `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`.
- The native iOS/macOS clients (ADR-0024) have to store a permanent secret on the device.

## Goal

Let every API interface authenticate with short-lived OAuth 2.1 access tokens instead of static keys: the REST/OpenAPI surface, the MCP sidecar, and the first-party clients. Static API keys keep working during and after the transition unless the maintainer decides otherwise in the ADR.

## Scope

In scope (to be designed here, decided in the ADR):

- **Token issuance and validation.** Authorization code + PKCE for interactive clients (browser, iOS/macOS, MCP clients); a non-interactive grant for service callers (client credentials or device flow for CLIs). No implicit or password grant.
- **Resource-server behaviour** on `/api` and on the MCP sidecar: `WWW-Authenticate` challenge, RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata, RFC 8414 authorization-server metadata, audience binding (RFC 8707) so a token for one resource is not accepted by another.
- **Mapping a token to a Victual user.** Everything downstream (`User::GetPermissions()`, ADR-0018 role grants, audit attribution) already assumes a user row; the token must resolve to one.
- **Scopes.** How token scopes relate to the key-scoped permissions proposed in ADR-0044 and plan 37. Effective rights should remain the intersection of owner permissions and granted scope, so a token can never exceed its user.
- **Lifetime and revocation.** Access-token TTL, refresh-token rotation, revocation, and where token state lives (ADR-0007: auth state must outlive the process; the MCP sidecar must stay stateless and run as two replicas).
- **MCP.** The sidecar becomes a real resource server rather than a header-forwarder. §4.1 already anticipates this; the authorization spec revision current at the time must be re-read, not taken from that document.
- **Client management UI** analogous to the manage-API-keys dialog: which clients hold grants, revoke, last used.

Out of scope here: federation with an external identity provider (follow-up issue), user provisioning from an IdP, SAML.

## The decision that gates everything else

**Who is the authorization server?** This must be settled first because it shapes the follow-up issue.

1. **Victual issues its own tokens** (embedded authorization server). Self-contained for a household with no IdP; largest surface to build and secure in PHP; the sidecar validates against Victual.
2. **Victual is only a resource server** and trusts tokens from an external AS. Smallest Victual surface, but forces every deployment to run an IdP, which conflicts with the "works out of the box" default.
3. **Both:** a minimal built-in AS for standalone installs, replaceable by an external one via configuration.

My leaning is toward 3 with the interface between "validate a token, produce a user" kept narrow enough that the AS is swappable, but that is a hypothesis to test, not a decision. If option 2 or 3 is chosen the follow-up issue is substantially larger and may be worth doing first.

## Open questions

- Opaque tokens with introspection (RFC 7662) or signed JWTs? Introspection keeps revocation immediate but puts Victual on the MCP hot path; JWTs need a key-rotation story.
- Do we need dynamic client registration (RFC 7591) for MCP clients, or are pre-registered clients plus CIMD enough? Test against the actual Claude clients before building.
- Does PHP/Slim have a maintained library worth adopting (e.g. `league/oauth2-server`), and does it fit the license and the no-new-dependency posture in `docs/constitution.md`?
- Migration path for existing MCP-type and read-only keys, and whether a token inherits `read_only`.
- Threat model: token theft from native clients, CSRF on the consent screen, and the existing cross-origin check in `BaseAuthMiddleware`.

## Deliverables

1. Design discussion in this issue until the authorization-server question and the open questions above are answered.
2. **An ADR** recording the architecture (new decision; no existing record covers it). It builds on ADR-0007, ADR-0018 and ADR-0044 and would amend `docs/mcp-interface-spec.md` §4. It stays Proposed until the maintainer accepts it in its own PR.
3. A plan under `docs/plans/` once the ADR is accepted. No code before then.

## Related

- ADR-0044 / plan 37: per-key permission subsets (scope model should align)
- `docs/mcp-interface-spec.md` §4
- ADR-0007, ADR-0018, ADR-0024
- Follow-up: external IdP federation (OIDC/SAML, Authentik)

title: Users: roles can't be set when creating a user, and the only entry point is an unlabeled lock icon
body:
## Problem

There is no obvious way to set a user's role after (or while) creating them.

- The create/edit user form (`views/userform.blade.php`) has no role field, so roles cannot be chosen at creation.
- Roles are assigned only on `/user/{id}/permissions` (Roles multi-select, \"Save roles\"). The only link to it is the button in `views/users.blade.php` (~line 70) with a `fa-lock` icon and the tooltip \"Configure user permissions\". A lock reads as \"account locked\", not \"roles\".
- The Roles column in the users table is read-only text, so it does not suggest it is clickable.
- The button is hidden when `VICTUAL_IS_EMBEDDED_INSTALL` or `VICTUAL_DISABLE_AUTH` is set, which is correct but invisible to the user.

The API already supports this (`PUT /api/users/{userId}/roles`, body `{\"roles\":[ids]}`), so this is UI only.

## Proposed

1. Add a Roles multi-select to the user form. On create, save the user, then `PUT /users/{id}/roles`. Show it only to users who may administer that account (`USERS_EDIT` plus `User::MayAdminister`), matching the permissions page.
2. Replace the lock icon with `fa-user-shield` or `fa-user-tag` and retitle the tooltip \"Roles & permissions\".

## Acceptance

- A user with edit rights can pick roles in the create form and the new user has them after one submit.
- The users list button is recognisable as roles/permissions.
- Test covers create-with-roles and the denied case (no `USERS_EDIT`).

Found on branch `claude/user-role-after-creation-3a7f89`; not yet verified by running the app.

title: Consumption recipe sharing: answer a share request identically whether or not the user exists
body:
Found while implementing #698 (PRs #735 and #736). \`POST /api/consumption/recipes/{recipeId}/shares\` accepts a \`username\` or a \`user_id\`. A caller who owns the recipe or holds its share right gets 422 for an unknown name, 422 for the owner's name, and 204 for a known one, so usernames can be tested one at a time. ADR-0040 does not address it; ADR-0006 puts authenticated issues in scope.

Maintainer decision, 2026-10-09: accepted for v0.5.0 because this is a LAN service where any member can guess another member's name. The fix is wanted afterwards and is simple.

## Chosen fix

An authenticated caller who passes the existing checks (the \`STOCK_VIEW\` gate, the recipe exists and the caller holds the share right) always gets **204** from \`POST .../shares\`, whether or not the named user exists. A request without a valid token gets 401, as every route does today. An unknown user, the owner's own name, and a user the caller may not grant to all produce the same answer, and only a real, shareable user gets a share row.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] \`POST .../shares\` answers 204 for an unknown \`username\`, an unknown \`user_id\`, the owner's name, and a real user. No response body, header or timing step the tests can measure differs between them.
- [ ] Only the last case writes a share row. Tests assert row counts for all four.
- [ ] 401 without a token and 404/403 for a recipe the caller cannot use are unchanged.
- [ ] The rights rules of ADR-0040 rules 3 and 4 still apply to a real user: a grantor who tries to grant a right they lack still gets 403, because that answer depends on the caller's own rights and not on the target.
- [ ] \`PUT .../shares/{userId}\` and \`DELETE .../shares/{userId}\` are checked for the same oracle (a nonexistent user id versus an existing user with no share) and made uniform or the difference is documented.
- [ ] The page (\`public/viewjs/consumptionrecipes.js\`) reloads the share list after a request and says nothing about whether the user was found. The manual and \`victual.openapi.json\` (the \`204\` description) say that a 204 does not confirm the user exists.
- [ ] A contract snapshot, the API test and the browser probe cover the change.

## Consequence to record

The owner can no longer tell a typing mistake from a success by the status code. The share list is the confirmation. That is the intended trade.

title: Implement Home Assistant add-on version upgrades independently of Grocy import
body:
## Required outcome

Implement and verify the Home Assistant add-on's version-upgrade lifecycle as required delivery work for #654. Fresh schema setup and ordinary Victual upgrades must work without installing or running the optional, one-time Grocy import add-on.

This is an implementation tracker, not a reminder or a completed design. #654 must not be considered delivered until this work has implementation and verification evidence.

## Existing behavior and constraint

Repository inspection on 2026-10-04 at `43deecab70a13cedc7611004cc07f56228354c4a` found:

- `bin/victual-db-import` imports a SQLite database. #484 separately tracks the web setup/import flow.
- `bin/victual-migrate` initializes or upgrades the PostgreSQL schema. It serializes concurrent runs with a PostgreSQL advisory lock and is a no-op when the schema is current.
- `MIGRATE_ON_ROOT_REQUEST` defaults to false. `SchemaVersionMiddleware` refuses incompatible schemas. Therefore removing a separate upgrade container does not eliminate the need to execute schema upgrades.
- The existing Kubernetes deployment uses a migration init container. The HA target needs its own execution path within the main add-on lifecycle; it must not inherit a dependency on the Grocy import add-on.
- Accepted ADR-0010 requires least-privilege identities. The serving application must not gain DDL rights. Credentials in `/data/options.json` or another shared readable file remain accessible even if removed from a child process's environment; environment filtering alone does not prove isolation.

## Execution sequence

1. Design the main add-on's startup/upgrade execution and credential isolation against Supervisor's actual process, filesystem, and privilege controls. Identify required ADR changes; obtain acceptance through the separate lifecycle PR before shipping any exception.
2. Implement option validation, bounded PostgreSQL readiness handling, schema setup/upgrade execution, and serving-process startup only after successful completion. Reuse the existing migration service and locking behavior.
3. Define first-install, current-schema, older-schema, and newer-schema behavior. Fail closed on upgrade failure and incompatible newer schemas. Produce actionable logs without secrets.
4. Define upgrade coordination for any companion services that depend on schema/API compatibility. Do not assume image rollback reverses database changes.
5. Implement and run regression and Supervisor lifecycle tests, then document the supported operator procedure and recovery path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Record the execution and credential-isolation design, with any required ADR acceptance linked.
- [ ] Install on an empty PostgreSQL database without the Grocy import add-on.
- [ ] Upgrade a named previous Victual release without the Grocy import add-on; verify users, permissions, stock, uploaded files, and label data survive.
- [ ] Restart on a current schema without destructive changes or repeated bootstrap work.
- [ ] Verify simultaneous starts, PostgreSQL outage/recovery, interrupted execution, and a deliberately failing migration. No incompatible schema serves application traffic.
- [ ] Refuse a database newer than the deployed application with an actionable error.
- [ ] Prove serving processes cannot obtain elevated database credentials from environment, files, or other accessible process state and cannot execute DDL, unless a narrowly scoped exception has been explicitly accepted.
- [ ] Back up external PostgreSQL before an upgrade and demonstrate restoration with the matching application release. Explain what HA backups do and do not contain.
- [ ] Verify the actual Supervisor lifecycle on every advertised architecture. Record release versions, image digests, environment, and reproducible steps.
- [ ] Preserve the application coverage ratchet and report relevant test results in the implementation PR.
- [ ] Link the implementation PR and verification evidence here and in #654 before closing this issue.

## Scope boundary

This issue owns normal Victual schema setup and version upgrades for the HA target. It does not own Grocy data import, Ingress, a new migration framework, or changes to existing Kubernetes deployment behavior. Main add-on packaging and any required architecture decisions gate implementation; tracking this work does not accept the proposed combined nginx/PHP container design.

title: Feature Request: Target as Home Assistant Addon
body:
## Requested outcome

Add a supported Home Assistant add-on deployment target for Victual. A household should be able to install, configure, start, update, and recover Victual through Home Assistant, with documented database prerequisites and no local image build.

Original request: “Adding a target for the App to run as an HA add-on”. Home Assistant now calls add-ons “apps”; this issue retains “add-on” for continuity.

This is a deployment feature. MQTT entity publication already has its own work in [plan 18](https://github.com/datagen24/victual/blob/master/docs/plans/18-mqtt-state-publication.md) and #139. This issue does not replace that work or establish a new integration API.

## Required implementation work

- [ ] #655 implements schema setup and version upgrades independently of the Grocy import add-on. This is a release gate for this target. Close it only with linked implementation and verification evidence.

## Proposed first-release scope

- Target Home Assistant OS with Supervisor. Publish an installable repository entry, versioned prebuilt images, configuration schema, installation instructions, changelog, and recovery instructions. Choose and document minimum supported Home Assistant and Supervisor versions.
- Target `amd64` and `aarch64`, with installation and lifecycle evidence for each architecture before advertising support.
- Expose the web interface through Home Assistant Ingress. Verify login, navigation, redirects, static assets, uploads, and API requests under its path prefix. Keep ordinary Victual authentication and permissions unless a separately accepted design establishes identity mapping.
- Provide PostgreSQL, InfluxDB, and MQTT connection settings in the add-on configuration flow. Each service may run on the HA host or elsewhere on the LAN; do not hard-code local add-on addresses or require bundled services. PostgreSQL is required. Preserve the existing enable/disable settings for MQTT and InfluxDB. Validate enabled connections, keep credentials out of logs, and run in production mode.
- Map PostgreSQL host, port, database, and separate application/migration credentials to the existing settings. Expose the MQTT endpoint, credentials, TLS, and topic/discovery settings, and the InfluxDB URL, token, organisation, and bucket. Where the configuration flow accepts a URL, validate and map it to the existing runtime settings; MQTT currently uses separate host, port, and TLS fields. These are operator deployment settings, not new outbound-URL fields in the Victual application API.
- Handle initial schema setup and version upgrades through the main add-on lifecycle, without requiring the one-time Grocy import add-on. Complete required schema changes before readiness. Preserve the distinction between the schema-upgrade identity and the restricted serving identity; the mechanism for isolating those credentials remains design work. Report schema-upgrade or dependency failures through useful logs and unhealthy status. Define bounded retries and recovery after PostgreSQL becomes available.
- Treat the Grocy import add-on as an optional, one-time transfer tool. Fresh installations and ordinary Victual version upgrades must work without installing or running it.
- Deliver printing and MCP companion add-ons with the first release. Printing must cover both label rendering and physical delivery through the existing label subsystem. Decide whether renderer and delivery worker require separate add-ons during topology design; neither function is deferred. MCP must expose the existing supported MCP capabilities through a companion add-on.
- Give companion add-ons validated connection and credential settings, health checks, logs, and documented start/stop, upgrade, and recovery behavior. Preserve each worker’s existing authentication and least-privilege boundary. Document printer connectivity and any justified device permissions. MCP client access must work independently of the browser-only Ingress session.
- Document every required background task, including MQTT publication, and how the Supervisor deployment starts, stops, and monitors it. Printing and MCP are required deliverables; users need only enable the companions they use.
- Provide a tested backup and restore procedure covering the database, configuration, and any durable files. State exactly what a Home Assistant backup includes; an external PostgreSQL database needs an explicit backup procedure.

## Existing constraints and design work

[ADR-0008](https://github.com/datagen24/victual/blob/master/docs/adr/0008-postgresql-only-runtime-engine.md) requires PostgreSQL. SQLite remains an import format. Bundling upstream grocy's SQLite deployment is not a compatible implementation.

[ADR-0013](https://github.com/datagen24/victual/blob/master/docs/adr/0013-nix-built-container-images.md) requires Nix-built production images. Reuse the existing derivations and production dependencies. Home Assistant supports a prebuilt `image` reference, so its example Alpine Dockerfile is not a requirement. [ADR-0030](https://github.com/datagen24/victual/blob/master/docs/adr/0030-released-images-are-published-to-ghcr.md), covering release image publication, is still Proposed; do not treat its registry policy as accepted.

The [current deployment](https://github.com/datagen24/victual/blob/master/deploy/README.md) separates web, PHP application, and migration workloads. The web workload has no database credential, and the serving application cannot run DDL. A Supervisor target needs its own topology and lifecycle design; the existing pod manifest does not establish add-on compatibility or require a separate upgrade add-on. `bin/victual-migrate` performs schema setup/upgrades; `bin/victual-db-import` performs the SQLite import. These operations must remain distinct even where existing deployment tooling packages them in the same image.

[ADR-0010](https://github.com/datagen24/victual/blob/master/docs/adr/0010-workload-standard.md) requires non-root workloads, a read-only root filesystem, least-privilege identities, probes, and limits. Demonstrate how Supervisor preserves these properties. Any required exception needs an ADR before shipping. Do not assume a combined container, root startup script, or Docker socket access is acceptable.

Ingress is a specific compatibility risk: Home Assistant supplies `X-Ingress-Path`, while Victual's `VICTUAL_BASE_PATH` is currently a build input used to warm its route cache. Prove the path-handling design with an installation-specific prefix. Do not assume setting an environment variable fixes it. Restrict the ingress listener to the documented proxy source and do not trust equivalent headers on a direct listener.

## Open questions

1. Where do PostgreSQL, InfluxDB, and MQTT run?

   > **Response (maintainer, 2026-10-04):** All three service connections are configurable through the add-on configuration flow. PostgreSQL may run on the HA host or on the LAN. In the maintainer’s deployment, PostgreSQL runs on the LAN, while InfluxDB and MQTT run on the HA host as add-ons. Their endpoints must still be explicitly configurable. Packaging must not require these services to be bundled or co-located.
2. How are web, application, schema-upgrade execution, and required background workloads packaged and supervised while preserving credential boundaries? Which Supervisor restrictions require an architectural decision?

   > **Response (maintainer, 2026-10-04):** The migration add-on is for a one-time migration from Grocy. Victual version upgrades must not depend on that container. Package ordinary upgrade handling with the main add-on lifecycle; credential isolation and process supervision still need a design.
3. Must the first release be entirely installable on one Home Assistant appliance?

   > **Response:** The service-location decision above permits external PostgreSQL and configurable InfluxDB and MQTT endpoints. Document the service prerequisites and connection setup for both HA-hosted and LAN-hosted deployments.
4. Is Ingress-only access sufficient, or must mobile clients and other API consumers have a separately authenticated direct endpoint? Which access paths and TLS arrangements will be supported?
5. Where will printing and MCP run?

   > **Response (maintainer, 2026-10-04):** Printing and MCP companion add-ons are required. Deliver both with the HA target. Printing includes rendering and delivery; the exact renderer/worker packaging remains a topology decision. MQTT and InfluxDB endpoints and credentials remain configurable through the add-on configuration flow.
6. Where will the add-on repository and images be published, who maintains releases, and what is the supported update/recovery policy after a schema migration? Do not promise image downgrade without proving schema compatibility.

Record answers under their questions. New architectural decisions belong in ADRs; acceptance remains a separate bookkeeping-only PR. The implementation plan must identify its gates before implementation starts.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Resolve the remaining workload topology, access, and release questions in an implementation plan, with required ADRs accepted separately.
- [ ] Install the published add-on on clean Home Assistant OS instances for every advertised architecture, using only the documented prerequisites.
- [ ] Verify configurable PostgreSQL, MQTT, and InfluxDB connections with HA-hosted and LAN-hosted services. Include the maintainer’s topology: LAN PostgreSQL with MQTT and InfluxDB add-ons on the HA host. Verify endpoint changes, invalid credentials, TLS options where supported, disabled optional services, and recovery after connection loss.
- [ ] Complete a stock booking and retrieve it after add-on restart and host reboot; verify users, permissions, uploads, and labels already stored in the database survive.
- [ ] Exercise Ingress login/logout, redirects, assets, uploads, and representative read/write API requests. Verify an untrusted request cannot use ingress headers to bypass authentication or permissions.
- [ ] Verify invalid options, database outage, migration failure, unhealthy child processes, and stop/start behavior. The serving application must not receive migration credentials or serve an incompatible schema.
- [ ] Verify a fresh installation and an upgrade from a named previous release without the Grocy import add-on installed. Then restore a pre-upgrade backup into a fresh installation and verify its data. Document recovery when a downgrade is unsupported.
- [ ] Verify non-root execution, filesystem restrictions, minimum privileges, secret handling, health checks, and resource behavior on the actual Supervisor deployment.
- [ ] Add configuration/image checks and appropriate regression coverage to CI. Preserve the repository's coverage ratchet for application changes.
- [ ] Install and configure the printing companions, render a label, deliver it to a supported physical printer, and verify the resulting job status. Exercise printer unavailability and worker restart using existing lease/retry semantics; document uncertain delivery outcomes.
- [ ] Install and configure the MCP companion, connect a supported MCP client, and verify existing supported tools, permission enforcement, credential rejection, and reconnect after restart.
- [ ] Verify companion compatibility across a main add-on upgrade, including behavior while the main service is unavailable. Coordinate schema/API compatibility with #655.
- [ ] Publish installation, configuration, backup, recovery, limitations, and troubleshooting instructions. Record tested versions, architectures, image digests, and reproducible verification steps.

## Research references

Repository assessment: 2026-10-04, working-copy HEAD `43deecab70a13cedc7611004cc07f56228354c4a`; inspection only, no Home Assistant deployment tested.

- [Home Assistant app configuration](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/apps/configuration/): prebuilt images, architectures, options, privileges, and persistent storage.
- [Home Assistant Ingress requirements](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/apps/presentation/#ingress): proxy restrictions and path handling.
- [Home Assistant app communication](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/apps/communication/): service communication and Supervisor access.

body:
## Summary

Add an installation country, stored as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (for example `US`). Several features need to know where the household shops, and today nothing records it. Grocy's only barcode source, inherited by this fork, assumes a European catalogue.

## Consumers
- **Plan 09 / #80:** the US barcode source. With the country set to `US`, USDA FoodData Central is tried before Open Food Facts. #80's pantry sampling is still outstanding, and this issue does not replace it.
- **Plan 34 / #483:** the installation default pattern for restricted-circulation (scale and deli) stickers. Plan 34's question 1 was answered to derive the default from the country. Until this setting exists, the default stays unset.
- **Default units of measure:** US customary for `US`, metric elsewhere. Quantity units are user-editable master data, so a country can only choose which units are seeded or suggested. Existing data is not converted.
- **Other candidate defaults:** `CURRENCY`, `DEFAULT_LOCALE`, `ENERGY_UNIT`, and the first day of the week. Each would be derived only when the administrator has not set it explicitly.

## How it can be set (operator, 2026-09-24): onboarding or an environment variable
- **Environment variable.** This needs almost no new code. `Setting('COUNTRY', '')` in `config-dist.php` is enough, because the existing `Setting()` override in `helpers/extensions.php` already reads `VICTUAL_COUNTRY` from the environment or from `settingoverrides/COUNTRY.txt`.
- **Onboarding (#484).** The wizard cannot write `config.php` or the environment. Production images run with a read-only root, and the Kubernetes deployment is configured entirely through `VICTUAL_*` variables. A value chosen in the wizard therefore needs a database home, such as an installation settings row.

## Open questions
1. **Precedence.** When both are set, which wins, the environment variable or the stored value? The proposal is that the environment variable wins and the wizard shows the country as locked. This matches how every other `Setting()` behaves under deployment.

   > **Response:**

2. **Derived defaults.** Are derived defaults computed at read time, where they follow the country if it changes, or written once when the country is first set? The proposal is read time, with an explicit setting always overriding a derived value.

   > **Response:**

3. **Unset country.** When no country is set, does behaviour stay exactly as today (Open Food Facts only, no default pattern), or does the wizard require a country? The proposal is to keep today's behaviour when unset, and have the wizard ask for a country but not require one.

   > **Response:**

## Related
#80 (plan 09), #483 / #485 (plan 34, ADR-0031), #484 (web setup flow).

## Summary

Add a web setup flow for bringing up Victual. The admin uploads a grocy database through a form, and a setup wizard takes the app from a fresh install to ready. This is a stub that records the flow so it stops living only in memory. The design is not started.

## Current behaviour
- **Importing a grocy database is CLI-only.** It runs through `bin/victual-db-import` (plan 24, `docs/plans/landed/24-sqlite-runtime-retirement.md`), which means shell access to the container or host.
- **The only first-run flow is the forced admin password change** (`must_change_password`, from the bootstrap-admin work). It gates the API until the admin changes the generated password.
- **Nothing records this work.** No plan, ADR or issue covers a web import or setup wizard. Searched: `docs/plans`, `docs/adr`, and the tracker for wizard, onboarding, db-import and "import grocy".

## Intended flow (operator, 2026-09-24)
1. The admin uploads the grocy SQLite database through a form.
2. The import runs through the same code as `bin/victual-db-import`.
3. A setup wizard walks the admin through whatever the import cannot decide alone, then brings the app up.

## First known consumer
The barcode conflicts page from #483, as a *possible* host, not a dependency. Canonicalising barcodes can collide rows the old raw index allowed, for example `012345678905` and `0012345678905` on two different products. Rows like these, and codes whose check digits fail, need an admin decision.

**Update, 2026-09-24 (#483 rev 3):**
- #483 now **quarantines only the affected codes**, holding a per-identity reservation, and ships its own admin conflicts page **before** this flow exists.
- Barcode conflicts therefore **no longer require a global setup gate.** This wizard may later host the same conflicts page as a step.
- Running an import may still need a **separate maintenance state**, one that holds writes while the grocy database is being loaded. That is this issue's question (Q3), not #483's.

## Open questions
1. **Upload limits.** A grocy database with images can be large, and the upload clamp (#217) applies. Does the upload go through `FILE_STORAGE`, or is it streamed?

   > **Response:**

2. **Upgrades.** Does the wizard also run on an upgrade that introduces a step needing a decision, as #483 needs? Or is it first-run and import only?

   > **Response:**

3. **Maintenance state during import.** Barcode conflicts no longer need a gate (see above). Does *running* an import need a maintenance state that refuses writes, or the whole API, until the load finishes? If so, should it be modelled on the `must_change_password` gate?

   > **Response:** Yes, scoped to import execution only (datagen24, 2026-09-24). The maintenance state covers the running import and nothing else. Barcode conflicts are handled by #483's quarantine and do not need it. This issue proceeds independently of #483 and plan 34.
